about: Reviewed explanatory content for the C3 Migration Studio PP1 views. Text only: it holds no research numbers. Every number shown next to this text is computed by scripts/summarize_evidence.py and components/c3_data_layer/dashboard/pp1_content.py from committed evidence or the fresh current-code run, and carries its source. Text is taken from docs/C3_PP1_audit_inventory.md (read-only audit, verified against the source) and docs/c3_fr_status.json.
methodology: Requirement text is quoted verbatim from the proposal as extracted in docs/C3_audit_2026-10-17.md; statuses and limitations come from the reviewed file docs/c3_fr_status.json.
Every number is a referenced measurement or a computed count with its evidence file and derivation; select a value to open its evidence.

Stages are kept apart: historical evaluation files (pre-adaptation, post-adaptation, post-fix, fresh holdout) are never overwritten; current-code values come from a fresh run of the pipeline into a temporary folder outside the repository.
Restricted applications (HMS, Dignity-Dev, Fee-Rainbow, ams-native) are shown as counts and query IDs only: no SQL text, PHP source, schema data or reason text that quotes their source.

Conversion is not behavioural equivalence. Passing through the converter shows that a function was generated under the safety rules; behaviour is shown only where E1 or the Clinic MySQL verification ran.
Coverage figures are never called accuracy: recovery precision and recall are measured against author-verified ground truth; conversion coverage only counts generated functions.

FR1.purpose: Find every place where the legacy PHP sends SQL to MySQL, so that nothing is migrated blind.
FR1.implementation: A PHP extractor built on the nikic/php-parser AST walks every PHP file and reports each database execution call with its file, line, executor and SQL-argument expression. Single-parameter wrapper functions that forward their argument to an executor are detected, and calls to them become sites.
techniques: Executor tables for mysqli, mysql_* and PDO-style methods (query, prepare, exec)
Other DBMS APIs reported as UNSUPPORTED_EXECUTOR instead of ignored

demonstration.text: A mysqli_prepare call is detected and later converted.
Every live executor site in the ground truth is detected (see the detection measurement).

improvements.text: Wrapper-call detection and the SQL-fragment variable rule.
Correct PHP string escape decoding.
Prepared statements with ? and :name placeholders.

future: Multi-parameter wrapper functions and class-based database layers.
A benchmark application that uses PDO (PDO is covered by fixtures and unit tests only).

FR2.purpose: Rebuild the SQL text that the PHP constructs at run time, so it can be analysed and converted.
FR2.implementation: The assignment chain of the SQL variable is followed backwards through = and .= assignments; literals, concatenation, interpolation and array elements are rebuilt into a template with named placeholders for runtime values. SQL built and executed in the same conditional block is recovered. Chains that depend on which branch, loop iteration or switch case ran, or whose variables carry SQL text, are flagged UNRESOLVED with a reason code instead of guessed.
techniques: PHP string decoding (escapes, interpolation, array elements)
Guards: branching, loop/switch, structural placeholder, SQL-fragment variable
Query-specific templates for exact Clinic shapes (reported separately)

demonstration.text: Branch-dependent SQL abstains with BRANCHING; the ground truth classifies these sites as not recoverable.
Branch-dependent SQL rebuilt only by query-specific templates for those exact files.

improvements.text: SQL built and executed in the same conditional block (S13).
Array elements with literal keys recovered as named values.
Escape decoder.
SQL-fragment variable rule.

FR2.partial_reason: Against the ground truth every site judged recoverable is recovered; against the requirement wording, SQL whose text differs between branches is not rebuilt by a general rule (only the Clinic templates do), so the status stays Partial.
future: Loop-built SQL as an explicit batch statement (not planned).

FR3.purpose: Know the database structure the migrated code must target.
FR3.implementation: The MySQL schema file is stripped of comments, its CREATE TABLE bodies are parsed into columns, keys, defaults, constraints and indexes, and phpMyAdmin-style ALTER TABLE key and AUTO_INCREMENT statements are applied afterwards. Views, triggers, procedures, functions and events are recorded as unsupported objects.

demonstration.text: Tables, columns and declared foreign keys parsed into schema.json.

improvements.text: Recover ALTER TABLE keys; key-less tables become Core tables.
Never abort the pipeline on a column type.
Schema fidelity and robust relationships (S9).

future: Relationship inference for schemas without declared foreign keys (not planned).

FR4.purpose: Know which tables and columns each query reads, writes and filters.
FR4.implementation: Each recovered or converted statement is parsed with SQLGlot; tables and aliases are attributed, SELECT * is expanded against the schema, and columns are classified as read, write, filter, join, group, order or having.
techniques: Star expansion against the parsed schema

demonstration.text: Join, group and order columns across three tables.

improvements.text: Column-use roles, table attribution, star expansion and template column use (S11).

FR4.partial_reason: How result columns are used later in the PHP application logic is not traced, so the second half of the requirement is not implemented.
future: Trace fetched-row keys into later PHP use (deferred; it could change frozen HMS outputs).

FR5.purpose: Give the migrated application typed Python models of the existing database.
FR5.implementation: One SQLAlchemy ORM class per table with a primary key and a Core Table for tables without one; generic types are used where they are exact and MySQL variants where a generic type would change the column; TINYINT(1) becomes Boolean only for non-key columns; relationships come from foreign keys.
techniques: MySQL to SQLAlchemy type mapping with dialect variants
ORM class or Core Table selection

demonstration.text: models.py with ORM classes and foreign-key relationships.

improvements.text: Exact MySQL types where the generic type would change them.
TINYINT(1) is Boolean only for non-key columns.

future: ORM classes for key-less tables would need a chosen surrogate key (design decision, not planned).

FR6.purpose: Replace string-built SQL with parameterized SQLAlchemy functions where this is safe.
FR6.implementation: The recovered template is parameterized (quoted placeholders become named binds, LIKE wildcards are bound with the value), parsed with SQLGlot and accepted only if every placeholder is in a scalar value position. Multi-table SELECTs must satisfy the INNER JOIN rule or the LEFT/comma-join result-shape rule. One text() function with named binds is emitted per accepted site; the SQL text itself is unchanged.
techniques: Named bind parameters with SQLAlchemy text()
Standalone generated module with inlined helpers

demonstration.text: Two LEFT JOINs with COUNT, GROUP BY and ORDER BY, converted under the result-shape rule.
Implicit comma joins converted under the result-shape rule.
Recoverable LEFT JOIN that abstains because its tables are not in the parsed schema.

improvements.text: Prepared statements.
Transaction policy and LIMIT/OFFSET integer coercion.
Standalone generated data_access.py.
BETWEEN bounds and allow-listed function arguments as bound values.
LEFT JOIN and comma-join SELECTs under the result-shape rule.

FR6.partial_reason: One ground-truth recoverable site (Fee-Rainbow Q054) is not converted; behavioural equivalence is shown only for HMS (E1, with inconclusive sites) and Clinic; the INNER JOIN rule has no result-shape check, so converted star projections over joins are unverified.
future: Apply the result-shape check to INNER JOINs.
E1 behavioural runs for Dignity-Dev, Helpdesk and NEWS-BUZZ.

FR7.purpose: Make sure every runtime value reaches the database as a bound parameter, never as SQL text.
FR7.implementation: A placeholder is bound only in a scalar value position: comparison right-hand side, IN item, INSERT value, column plus value, BETWEEN bound, LIMIT or OFFSET, or the value argument of an allow-listed function. Identifiers and SQL fragments are flagged STRUCTURAL. The security report traces legacy user inputs to placeholders and scans the generated code for non-literal text() calls.

demonstration.text: ORDER BY bound to a schema allow-list (query-specific template).

improvements.text: Security report and schema-derived identifier allow-lists (S6).
Array-element parameters credited in the security report.
String-literal placeholder guard and extended value positions.

future: Runtime hostile testing on MySQL beyond HMS and the Clinic cases.
A converter-level guard for whole-list IN fragments (recovery blocks them today).

FR8.purpose: Never generate SQL that might be wrong: flag it for a person instead.
FR8.implementation: Every site that fails a recovery or conversion guard is written to unresolved_queries.json with its stage, reason code and reason, and receives a stub function that raises instead of generated SQL.

improvements.text: The unresolved report is one of the three primary outputs.

future: Per-reason manual-review guidance in the unresolved report itself.

FR9.purpose: Give the modernized data layer a managed starting point for future schema changes.
FR9.implementation: An Alembic environment (alembic.ini, env.py, script.py.mako) and an initial revision that creates every table in foreign-key dependency order are generated. Generating the files is not running a migration; the round trip was run separately in E3.

improvements.text: Alembic emitter as pipeline stage seven (S10).
env.py does not add the database password to SQLite URLs.

FR10.purpose: Let a reviewer go from any generated function back to the exact PHP line it replaces.
FR10.implementation: Each site keeps its file and line through every stage; traceability_report.json maps file:line to recovery status, conversion status and rule, and the generated function name and kind; generated docstrings carry the source label.
techniques: Source labels relative to the PHP root

improvements.text: Traceability report as a pipeline output (S12).
HMS handoff package with frozen signatures.

future: Regenerate the HMS handoff document after the frozen tag (its Q036 label omits the include directory).

STRUCTURAL:dynamic_table.meaning: A variable supplies a table name.
STRUCTURAL:dynamic_table.why: Identifiers cannot be bound as parameters, and writing them into the SQL would let input choose the table.
STRUCTURAL:dynamic_table.review: List the possible table values and write one function per table, or bind an allow-list.
STRUCTURAL:dynamic_table.future: Generalise the Clinic Q013 schema allow-list.

STRUCTURAL:dynamic_order_by.meaning: A variable supplies an ORDER BY column.
STRUCTURAL:dynamic_order_by.why: A sort column is an identifier, not a value.

STRUCTURAL:in_list_fragment.meaning: A variable holds a whole comma-separated IN list.
STRUCTURAL:in_list_fragment.why: The list is SQL text, not one value.
STRUCTURAL:in_list_fragment.review: Confirm the element type and use an expanding bind.
STRUCTURAL:in_list_fragment.future: Generalise the Clinic Q011 expanding bind.

STRUCTURAL:sql_fragment.meaning: A variable carries SQL clause text.
STRUCTURAL:sql_fragment.why: The variable changes the statement itself, so it cannot be bound.
STRUCTURAL:sql_fragment.review: Rebuild the clause logic by hand.

BRANCHING.meaning: The SQL text depends on which branch ran.
BRANCHING.why: Different branches build different statements; no single safe statement exists.
BRANCHING.review: Review each variant and write one function per variant.

LOOP_OR_SWITCH_CONTROL_FLOW.meaning: The SQL is built across loop iterations or depends on which switch case ran.
LOOP_OR_SWITCH_CONTROL_FLOW.why: The statement shape depends on run-time iteration.
LOOP_OR_SWITCH_CONTROL_FLOW.review: Rewrite as an explicit statement or batch.

UNKNOWN_EXPR:unsupported_expression.meaning: The SQL is built with a PHP expression the recovery does not model.
UNKNOWN_EXPR:unsupported_expression.why: The value or text of the expression cannot be determined statically.
UNKNOWN_EXPR:unsupported_expression.review: Read the PHP and rewrite the call.

UNKNOWN_EXPR:no_assignment_chain.meaning: No assignment that builds the SQL argument was found.
UNKNOWN_EXPR:no_assignment_chain.why: The SQL variable is set somewhere the recovery does not follow. The recovery record has no code; the unresolved report assigns UNKNOWN_EXPR as its fallback.
UNKNOWN_EXPR:no_assignment_chain.review: Find where the variable is set.

UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE.meaning: The recovered text is not a recognised CRUD statement.
UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE.why: For example SHOW, an empty string or a non-SQL value.
UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE.review: Usually none: administrative or dead SQL.

MISSING_SQL_ARGUMENT.meaning: The SQL argument of the call could not be identified.
MISSING_SQL_ARGUMENT.why: The call has no recognisable SQL argument.

MULTI_STATEMENT_EXECUTOR.why: Several statements cannot become one parameterized statement.

CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:join_schema.meaning: A LEFT JOIN or comma join whose tables are not in the parsed schema.
CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:join_schema.why: The result row keys cannot be checked without the table definitions.
CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:join_schema.review: Supply the complete schema and re-run.

CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:join_other.meaning: A LEFT JOIN or comma join failing another result-shape condition.
CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:join_other.why: Row keys would be unknown or could collide.

CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:multi_table.meaning: A multi-table form outside the join rules.

CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:placeholder_posit.meaning: A runtime value in a position that is not a scalar value.
CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:placeholder_posit.why: Binding it would change the statement structure.
CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:placeholder_posit.review: Rewrite with an allow-list or by hand.

CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED:other.meaning: Another conversion guard failed (parse error, operation, prepared placeholders, binding plan).

recoverable_unsupported.label: Recoverable but unsupported
recoverable_unsupported.text: The ground truth says the site is recoverable, but C3 does not convert it.

non_recoverable.label: Non-recoverable under the current ground truth
non_recoverable.text: The ground truth classifies the site as abstain; C3 abstaining is a correct abstention.

ambiguous.label: Ambiguous
ambiguous.text: The ground truth could not decide; such sites are excluded from precision and recall.

non_live.label: Non-live
non_live.text: Commented-out or dead code; detected but excluded from live-site denominators.

unverified.label: Unverified
unverified.text: Generated but its behaviour or result shape has not been verified.

failed_verification.label: Failed verification
failed_verification.text: A verification ran and failed; none in the final evidence.

verification_inconclusive.label: Verification inconclusive
verification_inconclusive.text: E1 could not decide (for example no differing data); inconclusive is not a pass.

schema_mismatch.label: Schema mismatch
schema_mismatch.text: The site references tables or columns that are not in the supplied schema file.

measurement_definitions.title: Dignity-Dev: three denominators
measurement_definitions.text: Migration Impact shows converted sites of all detected sites (the detected count includes the non-live Q010). Conversion coverage counts converted ground-truth recoverable sites of all recoverable sites. The manual-review proxy counts live sites not converted of all live sites.

measurement_definitions.title: Fee-Rainbow: converted functions versus coverage
measurement_definitions.text: Converted functions count every generated function, including an ambiguous ground-truth site. Coverage counts only recoverable sites.

measurement_definitions.title: Clinic: templates and recovered counts
measurement_definitions.text: Query-specific templates convert sites that general recovery leaves unresolved, so converted can exceed recovered. The general-rule share is reported separately.

measurement_definitions.title: HMS E1 versus Clinic MySQL verification
measurement_definitions.text: E1 compares the legacy PHP-built SQL with the generated function per site on MySQL, for HMS only; inconclusive is not a pass. The Clinic MySQL verification is a separate pytest suite: tests that run the Clinic application's own PHP against the generated functions, plus join-rule tests that run the same SQL directly through PHP mysqli against the generated function. Neither is the other.

measurement_definitions.title: Regression totals
measurement_definitions.text: The non-MySQL suite and the full suite with MySQL run the same test tree; the skipped non-MySQL tests are the tests that need MySQL, and the Clinic suite is counted inside the full suite. Older saved logs are shown as history.

measurement_definitions.title: E4 bounded check
measurement_definitions.text: Every generated function is called with fixed hostile payloads in a recording session; SQL is compiled for MySQL but never executed. Functions that take no runtime value have no payload cases and pass trivially; they are counted separately below.

measurement_definitions.title: Schema completeness
measurement_definitions.text: E2 compares the schema views; it cannot show that a schema file is complete. Fee-Rainbow's supplied schema defines one table, and sites referencing other tables are listed as schema mismatch.

measurement_definitions.title: Verification not performed
measurement_definitions.text: Applications with no E1 run are listed in the E1 card; conversion alone does not show behavioural equivalence.
